name: Gap-up fade overlay
tagline: Overlay on the winner: fade small gap-ups in a weak tape, then re-enter before the close.
summary: Standalone gap strategies fail because TQQQ's drift is overnight and intraday-only gap trades make only 2-9% CAGR. On top of the 165-day QQQ regime and the armed 4% minute stop, selling TQQQ at 09:31 on armed +0.15% to +0.50% gap-ups and buying back at 15:59 lifts 10-year CAGR from 58.80% to 65.17% and cuts max drawdown from 44.56% to 39.02%. The 5-year result is 54.92%/30.99%, but it is fragile to the arm-gate buffer and the per-event edge is not statistically significant.
decision_process: At 09:30 ET the strategy reads QQQ's opening gap (open vs prior close) and the first-minute close. If QQQ's prior close is above its 165-day SMA (risk-on), the 4% stop is armed when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01, and the gap is between +0.15% and +0.50%, it targets 100% BIL for the 09:30 bar; the harness fills at the 09:31 open. At 15:58 it targets 100% TQQQ for the 15:59 open unless TQQQ closed 4% below the session open at any bar through 15:58, in which case it stays in BIL overnight. Otherwise the base winner holds TQQQ overnight and uses the 4% armed stop.
rules: Regime: QQQ's prior daily close above its 165-day SMA means risk-on; otherwise hold 100% BIL.
On risk-on days, hold 100% TQQQ including overnight.

Arm the 4% stop only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01. While armed, if TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.
Gap-up fade: on a risk-on, armed day with a QQQ opening gap between +0.15% and +0.50% versus the prior close, sell TQQQ at the 09:31 open and hold 100% BIL through 15:58.
Re-enter at the 15:59 open unless TQQQ closed 4% below the session open at any bar through 15:58; if it did, stay in BIL overnight.
Next session: re-enter at the open if the regime is still on. Long-only, no leverage beyond 1x TQQQ, no shorting.
verdict: Strictly dominates the winner at 1 bp and 5 bp on both windows (65.17/39.02 and 54.92/30.99 at 1 bp; 58.02/40.93 and 48.78/31.65 at 5 bp), but the 5-year pass depends on the winner's exact 1% arm gate and collapses at 0.5%/1.5%, and the per-event edge is not significant (t=1.60 over 10y, 0.92 over 5y). Treat the 10-year result as a robust crash-hedge overlay and the 5-year result as sample-specific.

sources.idea: Small opening gaps fill; large gaps persist and continue. This size split is the reason to fade only the small-gap band and exclude large gap-ups.
sources.source: MPM Markets (2026) / Testing the 'Gaps Always Fill' Myth Across Six Futures Markets
sources.evidence: Small gaps fill quickly and almost always during the same session; large gaps often remain unfilled for several sessions and continue; the study finds no reliable edge after costs. Used to justify the 0.15-0.50% fade band and to exclude >1% gaps.

sources.idea: NQ/ES same-session gap-fill probability falls monotonically with gap size; big gaps are continuation, not fade.
sources.source: Steady Turtle (2026) / How often does the gap fill? NQ & ES, six years of data
sources.evidence: NQ same-session fill 60.3%; sub-10-point gaps 96.4%, 80-point-plus gaps 38.1%. The article explicitly concludes that big gaps are continuation and small gaps are where the fade lives. Used for the size split and the 0.15-0.50% band.

sources.idea: Gap-fill probability scales with volatility: gaps under 0.25x ATR fill about 94% of the time; gaps over 2x ATR fill about 9%.
sources.source: Open Market Journal (2026) / Does the S&P 500 Fill Its Gaps? It Depends on Size
sources.evidence: Same-session fill rates by ATR bucket. The 0.15-0.50% QQQ gap is roughly 0.10-0.34x the local median 14-day ATR of 1.49%, inside the high-fill region; >1% gaps are outside it.

sources.idea: Large up-gaps (2%+) fill only about 27% of the time same-day and have positive open-to-close drift; 1%+ up-gaps are continuation, not fade.
sources.source: thetrading.tools (2026) / Gap Analysis: Do Gaps Always Fill? SPY & QQQ
sources.evidence: 2%+ up-gap same-day fill 27%, 52% within five sessions; 1%+ up-gaps average a positive open-to-close return with about a 60% up-day rate. Used to exclude large gap-ups from the fade.

sources.idea: Small up-gaps usually close same-session; large +2%+ up-gaps mostly do not; up-gaps fill faster than down-gaps.
sources.source: IOSR Journal of Economics and Finance (2019) / Filling Open Price Gap on Intraday Timeframe: A Case Study for DJIA Index Stocks
sources.evidence: 68.2% of small up-gaps close same-session; only 12.1% of +2%+ up-gaps close; 50% of up-gaps close by 09:52 and 50% of down-gaps by 11:08. Used for the early-session fade window and the size split.

sources.idea: Positive gaps drift in the gap direction, while negative gaps are larger and adjust faster. Supports keeping large gap-ups as continuation and treating the fade as a small-gap, positive-gap phenomenon.
sources.source: Aiche, Cohen & Griskin (2024) / Stocks Opening Price Gaps and Adjustments to New Information, Computational Economics 63
sources.evidence: Ten years of S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and Russell 2000 stocks: negative gap openings are larger, bad-news adjustment is quicker, and positive gaps drift. Used as background for the asymmetry and the large-gap continuation side.

sources.idea: Gap-day prices tend to move in the gap direction; the momentum effect is temporary; the naive 'gaps always fill' rule is false.
sources.source: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance (2020) / Price gap anomaly in the US stock market: The whole story
sources.evidence: 1928-2018 DJI, S&P 500 and Nasdaq: prices change in the gap direction on the gap day; no evidence that gaps always fill. Used to motivate testing continuation and the size split rather than a blanket fade.

sources.idea: Intraday reversals after large opening changes exist, are stronger after large positive changes, and shrink after bid-ask costs.
sources.source: Grant, Wolf & Yu (2005) / Intraday price reversals in the US stock index futures market: A 15-year study, Journal of Banking & Finance 29(5)
sources.evidence: S&P 500 futures, 1987-2002: significant intraday reversals after large opening gaps, stronger after positive gaps; profits are sharply reduced by a bid-ask proxy. Supports the fade direction and the cost caution.

sources.idea: The opening auction aggregates overnight information; the opening price is a meaningful signal, though it can also reflect stabilization and non-information factors.
sources.source: Review of Financial Studies 13(3) (2000) / Price Discovery in Auction Markets: A Look Inside the Black Box
sources.evidence: Opening mechanisms aggregate overnight information; the specialist's opening trade can reflect non-informational stabilization requirements. Used as background for why the opening gap carries information.

sources.idea: Opening procedures and call auctions incorporate overnight information; opening volume predicts daytime volume and opening trades show price reversals.
sources.source: Gross (2003) / Price Discovery in Opening Procedures: The Efficiency of NYSE and Nasdaq Openings after Delays
sources.evidence: NYSE/Nasdaq openings after delayed openings: overnight information is incorporated in the opening procedure. Background only; no parameter was taken from it.

sources.idea: Opening call auctions affect ongoing trade; opening volume is related to daytime volume and opening trade prices show reversals.
sources.source: Journal of Financial Markets (2004) / The interaction between opening call auctions and ongoing trade: Evidence from the NYSE
sources.evidence: Opening batch volume predicts volume across the day; opening trade price reversals; the opening process handles information efficiently. Background only.

sources.idea: High overnight returns negatively predict the first half-hour return; the reversal strengthens during market stress.
sources.source: Does overnight return predict the first half-hour return for U.S. market indices? (2026)
sources.evidence: SPY: the overnight return negatively predicts the first 30-minute return; the reversal is stronger in high-volatility periods including the early COVID phase. This is the closest external support for fading a gap-up at the open.

sources.idea: The first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return (intraday momentum), stronger on volatile and macro-news days.
sources.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) / Market intraday momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 129(3)
sources.evidence: Used to check whether the gap signal was just intraday momentum. The overlay is an open-to-close fade, not a last-half-hour timing rule, so this paper did not determine the rule.

sources.idea: Trading costs can erase short-term reversal profits; better portfolio construction can preserve some of them.
sources.source: Journal of Banking & Finance (2012) / Another look at trading costs and short-term reversal profits
sources.evidence: Reversal profits can survive costs with better portfolio construction; conventional cost estimates can be misleading. Used for the 1/5/10 bp cost sensitivity and the warning that the standalone gap fades are cost-fragile.

sources.idea: Base 165-day QQQ SMA regime and armed 4% minute stop.
sources.evidence: The regime and stop are inherited from the round-1 winner; this agent only adds the gap overlay. The winner is reproduced exactly at 58.80%/44.56% (10y) and 49.88%/33.49% (5y) at 1 bp.

sources.idea: The exact +0.15% to +0.50% band, the armed-day gate, and the 15:59 stop-aware re-entry.
sources.evidence: The event study on local QQQ/TQQQ 1-minute data selected the band and the re-entry filter. The gap-band plateau in the report shows the neighbouring bands; no external source specifies these exact parameters.

sources.idea: Long-only, 1x TQQQ maximum, next-bar-open fills, and 1/5/10 bp costs.
sources.source: Own test / no external source (mandate and research/bt.py harness)
sources.evidence: The round-2 mandate caps weights at 1.0 and requires next-bar fills and cost stress; the shared bt.py harness supplies the fills and slippage. No external source determines these values.

rejected_sources.source: Loomi (2026) / Gap Fill Strategy: NQ Opening Gap Statistics
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested as a standalone gap-fade rule and rejected: 3,236 NQ trades, 2010-2026, three of four gap-size buckets lose after 1 point of costs; small gaps are the worst. This agrees with the report's negative standalone result and is the reason the gap signal is used only as an overlay.

rejected_sources.source: Rosa (2022) / Understanding intraday momentum strategies, Journal of Futures Markets
rejected_sources.why_rejected: The overnight-to-last-half-hour predictability disappears out of sample. Used only as a caution against treating the gap signal as a stable intraday predictor; no rule was derived from it.

rejected_sources.source: QuantifiedStrategies / Gap Reversal (currently listed on the web page)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Not used in this report. It is a generic retail gap-reversal page with no specific evidence or parameter that entered the overlay; the page's attribution is inaccurate.

rejected_sources.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) / A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns (currently listed on the web page)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Not used directly in this report. It supports the general overnight/intraday reversal idea, but the direct overnight-reversal source here is the 2026 paper; no rule or parameter was taken from Lou et al.

rejected_sources.source: Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008) / Like Night and Day (currently listed on the web page)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Not used in this report. It is background on overnight versus intraday returns; no rule, parameter or test was derived from it. The web page's attribution is inaccurate.

rejected_sources.source: Naive 'gaps always fill' rule (folk rule tested against MPM Markets, Steady Turtle and Open Market Journal)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Rejected by the local event study: large gap-ups (>1%, especially >2%) continue rather than fill, and the small-gap fade is too small to beat TQQQ standalone. The report fades only the 0.15-0.50% band and leaves large gaps alone.

rejected_sources.source: Zarattini & Aziz (2023) / Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? Opening Range Breakout
rejected_sources.why_rejected: The ORB continuation variant was tested on this data and failed to beat TQQQ standalone (best ORB30 +2% gap-up: 4.54%/4.96% 10y, 4.81%/4.96% 5y). Not used. The paper's TQQQ result uses 2-4x intraday notional, which this long-only 1x harness does not allow.

corrections: Status: change 'Verified' to 'Fragile'. The 5-year strict dominance holds only at the winner's exact 1% arm gate; at 0.5%/1.5% buffers the 5-year CAGR falls to about 45%, and the per-event edge is not statistically significant (t=1.60 over 10y, 0.92 over 5y).
Metrics: add the measured 5 bp row. cagr10_5bp=0.5802, dd10_5bp=0.4093, cagr5_5bp=0.4878, dd5_5bp=0.3165. The current page only shows the 1 bp metrics.
Tagline: 'Fade small gap-ups when the tape is weak; re-enter before the close' reads as a standalone strategy. It is an overlay on the 165-day QQQ regime plus the armed 4% stop; reword to say so.

Rules: the current three bullets omit the base regime and the armed 4% stop. Add: prior QQQ close above the 165-day SMA; 4% stop armed when QQQ's first-minute close is below prior MA20 x 1.01; stop sells at the next minute and stays out for the day and night.

Papers: remove 'QuantifiedStrategies - Gap Reversal', 'Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019)' and 'Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008)'. None was used in this report. The direct overnight-reversal source is the 2026 paper; the gap-size sources are MPM Markets, Steady Turtle, Open Market Journal, thetrading.tools, IOSR and Springer.
Report section 3: the gap-down bounce range is written '+0.13% to +0.34%'; the <-2% bucket is +0.11%, so the range is '+0.11% to +0.34%'.
Report section 2: 'at most ~4-5.5%/yr' mixes the regime-on subset (3.90%/5.46%) with the all-days intraday leg (6.25%/2.41%). Say which is which.
Report section 5.3: 'QQQ's first-minute price' should be 'QQQ's first-minute close'; the arm gate uses the 09:30 close, not the open.

Report section 9: 'excluding 2018/2021/2025 the overlay is roughly neutral' understates it. Those three years contribute 49.4% of the 63.8% total de-risk PnL, leaving about +1.9%/yr over the other seven years. Say 'most of the benefit', not 'neutral'.
Web page decision: specify that the gap and arm are known at the 09:30 close, the sell fills at the 09:31 open, and the 15:59 re-entry is set from the 15:58 close (not the 15:59 close).
Report section 5.1: 'hold 100% BIL until the close' is loose; it is BIL through 15:58 and TQQQ from the 15:59 open. Clarify.

Standalone table: the EOD, 10:30 time-exit, gap-up follow, ORB and prior-trend rows are from the research sweep with low-based stops; the shipped strategy.py reproduces the three gap-down VWAP rows. The web page should not imply every row is reproduced by strategy.py.
